Putting together all the measurements at z ∼ 5, spanning 2 decades in luminosity from L_IR ∼ 10^11 L_⊙ to L_IR ∼ 10^13 L_⊙, the data highlight a steeply increasing trend of the r_e,FIR − L_IR relation at L_IR < 10^12 L_⊙, followed by a downturn and a decreasing trend at brighter luminosities.

Finally, simulations that extend up to the stellar masses of the ALPINE galaxies considered in the present work predict a sub-set of galaxies (∼ 25 % at 10^10 M_⊙ < M_⋆ < 10^11 M_⊙) with sizes as large as those measured.
This suggests that the model from Popping et al. (2022) could predict too compact FIR dust emission extension.

Finally, we find that the dust continuum sizes are very close to the optical ones, as predicted from the JWST mass−size relation, pointing towards a quite extended, disk-like star-formation region traced by the IR emission

all_quotes.loc: 3.2. FIR sizes versus IR luminosity and stellar masses
all_quotes.quote: Altogether, our results might suggest a variable trend of FIR luminosity as a function of size, that ranges from an increase for faint objects, a downturn at some characteristic luminosity of the order of 10^12 L_⊙, followed by a decreasing trend at brighter luminosities.

Altogether, the data samples considered in this work, spanning 2 dex in IR luminosity, highlight a variable trend in the r_e,FIR − L_IR relation, ranging from steeply increasing behaviour at L_IR < 10^12 L_⊙, followed by a downturn and a decreasing trend at brighter luminosities.

Moreover, our r_e,UV/r_e,FIR are significant smaller (up to a factor of 5-10) than the values predicted by the hydrodynamical cosmological simulations from Popping et al. (2022) and extrapolated at the stellar masses of our galaxies.

(2023) are predicted with large sizes, in the range of 1.5 − 4 kpc, populating the upper envelope of the distribution and in agreement with the ALPINE galaxies analysed in the present work.

The present study increases the number of sources with measured dust continuum sizes at very high z and, given the lower IR luminosity range spanned by the ALPINE galaxies, better constrains the r_e,FIR-L_IR scaling relation.
